messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: ensemble sampler interfaces
parts:
[off issue tracking, back on dev list]

On 5/17/13 11:47 AM, Peter Li wrote:
> Ah. One more issue: How exactly would we be able to run these different
> samplers simultaneously? One solution would be to define a new type in
> sample that would actually be a vector of samples. I feel like that
> would be the easiest that way we do not have to modify any of the other
> framework in gm/command.hpp.

These issues are partly why I thought it'd be a good time to
look at ensembles. If we want to do something like
parallel tempering we'll have similar design issues.

We definitely want to encapsulate the ensemble somehow
so we can pass it all around by reference.

For threading, the ensembles can be divided up into blocks which
can be independently updated (treating each block as its own
ensemble then recombining when done).

We should have a Rosenbrock banana-type density in our bag
of tests just to keep up with the Joneses. Michael B had
one in his Geometric NUTS paper --- don't know if it ever
made it into our source.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ensemble sampler interfaces
parts:
I'm also not sure how this will all play into R-hat
and auto-correlation evaluation. I think we need
to treat each walker in the ensemble like we treat
a chain now. I don't think it'll be kosher to just
scramble them together

As to convergence monitoring and effective sample size,
what we'll get looks like this:

walker1 ... walker N
-----------------------------
iteration 1 | theta[1,1] ... theta[1,N]
|
iteration m | theta[m,1] ... theta[m,N]

...

where theta[m,n] is a vector of all of our parameters for
the model.

I think we need to treat

theta[1,1], theta[2,1], theta[3,1], ...

like we currently treat a chain. That is, we can't scramble
the walkers, as in:

theta[1,1], theta[1,2], ..., theta[1,N], theta[2,1], theta[2,2], ...

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ensemble sampler interfaces
parts:
On 5/17/13 12:45 PM, Peter Li wrote:
> So if we can't scramble the walkers together at the end, what's the point of even running an ensemble sampler?

We scramble the walkers together for inference.

They discuss this in the paper --- it's affine invariant.
And also doesn't require gradients, like HMC does, so there's
an issue of speed. It's also easy to massively parallelize.

Some of the practical proponents claim it's also good for
mode-hopping, but we're skeptical.

We're also worried that in high dimensions, we'll need so many
walkers that just the convergence time will tank the overall
performance.

The big theoretical drawback to its adaptation is that it's global,
not local. So when you have something like the funnel,
it's still tricky because the geometry changes based
on whether you're in the neck of the wide part of the funnel.
You can also see this issue intuitively with the Rosenbrock
function. If you move between two members on different halves
of the banana, you won't wind up in a good space.

Looking on the bright side, there are still lots of nice
open research areas :-)

- Bob
